sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-398.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 398 was established by Ordinance No. 22054, passed by the Dallas City Council on May 25, 1994. Ordinance No. 22054 amended Ordinance No. 19455, Chapter 51A of the Dallas City Code, as amended. (Ord. Nos. 19455; 22054; 25850; 30490)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-398.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 398 is established on property generally located along the northwest line of Bryan Street, northeast of the northeast line of Peak Street. The size of PD 398 is approximately 0.39 acres. (Ord. Nos. 22054; 25850; 30490)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-398.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations contained in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this article, OUTDOOR COMMERCIAL AMUSEMENT means an event or gathering including one or more of the following activities:

(1) food and beverage sales in collaboration with an adjacent restaurant;

(2) art shows or craft shows;

(3) outdoor sport courts with portable seating, including sand volleyball courts and bocce ball courts; and

(4) exhibits or exhibitions that may involve erection of a temporary tent.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article refer to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. Nos. 22054; 25850; 30490)

SEC. 51P-398.103.1. EXHIBIT.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this article: Exhibit 398A: development/landscape plan. (Ord. 30490)

sections.title: Development/Landscape Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-398.104. DEVELOPMENT/LANDSCAPE PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the development/landscape plan (Exhibit 398A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article control. (Ord. Nos. 22054; 25850; 30490)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-398.105. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) The only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the MU-1 Mixed Use District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the MU-1 Mixed Use District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the MU-1 Mixed Use District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the MU-1 Mixed Use District is subject to DIR in this district; etc.

(b) The following uses are permitted by right:

-- Outdoor commercial amusement. -- Outside sales. (Ord. Nos. 22054; 25850; 30490)

SEC. 51P-398.105.1. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217. (Ord. 30490)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-398.106. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the MU-1 Mixed Use District apply.

(b) Setbacks. There are no minimum setbacks unless required by the visual obstruction regulations in Section 51A-4.602. (Ord. Nos. 22054; 25850; 30490)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-398.107. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Outdoor commercial amusement.

(1) One off-street parking space must be provided for every 100 square feet of non-permeable covered area shown on the development/landscape plan. Restroom facilities,

waitress stations, and storage areas are not included in the non-permeable covered area calculations.

(2) Outdoor seating areas that are uncovered or covered with a permeable cover are not included in required parking calculations, provided the seating area does not exceed 50 percent of the non-permeable covered area.

(3) Remote parking may be located on a separate lot that is within a 1,200 feet walking distance of the use served by the remote parking.

(A) The walking distance for remote parking may be extended beyond 1,200 feet by license as set out in Division 51A-4.320.

(B) An agreement authorizing remote parking for a use may be based on a lease of the remote parking spaces only if the lease:

(i) is in writing on a form obtained from the building official;

(ii) contains legal descriptions of the properties affected;

(iii) specifies the special parking being provided and the hours of operation of any use involved;

(iv) is governed by the laws of the State of Texas;

(v) is signed by all owners of the properties affected;

(vi) is signed by all lienholders, other than taxing entities, that have an interest in or an improvement on the properties;

(vii) is for a minimum term of three years; and

(viii) provides that both the owner of the lot occupied by the use benefitting from the parking and the owner of the remote parking lot shall notify the building official in writing if there is a breach of any provision of the lease, or if the lease is modified or terminated.

(C) A parking agreement is not required to be filed in the deed records if special parking is based on a lease approved by the building official.

(4) Except as expressly modified in this subsection, the special parking regulations in Division 51A-4.320 apply. If there is a conflict between this article and the special parking regulations, this article controls. (Ord. Nos. 22054; 25850; 30490)

SEC. 51P-398.107.1. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 30490)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-398.108. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Landscaping must be provided as shown on the development/landscape plan.

(b) Landscaping must be installed within six months after the issuance of a certificate of occupancy.

(c) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. Nos. 22054; 25850; 30490)

SEC. 51P-398.108.1. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for nonbusiness zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 30490)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-398.109. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) Outdoor commercial amusement.

(1) Revenue from an outdoor commercial amusement may be included when determining the gross revenue derived by an alcoholic beverage establishment or a restaurant from the sale of alcoholic beverages for on-premise consumption when:

(A) an outdoor commercial amusement is operating as a main use on a lot adjacent to an alcoholic beverage establishment or a restaurant use and a unified site plan has been approved by the building official; or

(B) an outdoor commercial amusement is accessory to an alcoholic beverage establishment or a restaurant use.

(2) An outdoor commercial amusement may only operate between 11:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m., Sunday through Thursday; and between 11:00 a.m. and 12:00 a.m. (midnight), Friday and Saturday.

(3) The portable seating area of an outdoor commercial amusement use may not exceed 875 square feet as shown on the development/landscape plan.

(b) Maintenance. The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(c) Compliance. Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 22054; 25850; 30490)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-398.110. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 22054; 25850; 30490)
